text: With suppliers configured, this lesson covers the other side of the business: the customers LTV sells to. One of these three customers, and one invoice created against it in Chapter 2, sits at the center of Chapter 3's AR investigation.

Three customers: Harborview Industrial Supply in Charlotte, North Carolina, and Tidewater Energy Systems in Norfolk, Virginia, both served by the US business unit; Great Lakes Automation Group in Ontario, served by the Canadian subsidiary and billed in CAD.

Harborview gets the full setup: customer type Distributor, one bill-to/ship-to site in Charlotte, Net 30 terms, a reviewed credit limit, and a remit-to address and receipt method configured so cash can be applied without manual lookup. Harborview already has order history, including an older open invoice that matters later.

Tidewater and Great Lakes Automation Group follow the same basic pattern — one site, standard profile class, Net 30 — without the extended history. A Receivables transaction can't exist without a customer, and cash can't be applied without a receipt method, so this setup comes before any invoicing.
Up next, lesson eight: configuring bank accounts and assets — the last piece of master data before Chapter 2 begins.
